references.text: Repeats that the remainder of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons, and is most holy.
Elaborates on the rules regarding the priests' portion of the grain offering, stating it is most holy and must be eaten by Aaron's sons.
Confirms that the grain offering belongs to the priest who presents it.
Moses instructs Aaron and his surviving sons to eat the remaining grain offering because it is most holy.
Notes that priests may eat from the most holy things and the holy things.
Describes how the most holy offerings, including the grain offering, belong to the priests.
Introduces the term 'most holy' (קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים) in connection with the altar.
Prophesies that priests shall eat the grain offering and everything dedicated to the Lord in Israel.
Refers to the sanctuary service of the old covenant and the holy things that point forward to Christ.
Lev 24:9 confirms and elaborates on the rule regarding who is to eat the most holy grain offering.
Numbers 18:9 expands the principle of the priest's right to most holy gifts to include all types of offerings.
Lev 6:11 clarifies which members of Aaron's lineage have the right to eat the holy things.
Lev 7:35 confirms that this portion of the offering is a perpetual right for the priest as a result of consecration.
Lev 6:9 specifies how and where the priest shall eat the remainder of the grain offering.
